summary.intent: Execute all plans (and then multiple gap-closure rounds) of GSD phase 68.1 for CipherBox — wiring the v2.0 web app onto the node/v3 read+write chain — driving through wave-based subagent orchestration until the full 208-spec web-e2e suite passes and every roadmap success criterion (WEB-01..WEB-04) is verified.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.1 executed across 33 plans and 3 gap-closure rounds spanning multiple sessions; e2e failures dropped from a 6/208 baseline through 17→13→8→5→0 real code failures (remaining failures are two explicitly human-approved deferrals: recovery.html v2-only blob format and rotation-durability SC-4's unreachable relay-replay). User-reported bugs (cold-reload subfolder navigation, text-editor decryption failure, move write-link orphaning, single-file-share editor) were root-caused and fixed with TDD regression tests. Verification round 3 scored 4/5 with one pending human decision on writable-shares 10.3/10.4 (subsequently fixed via plans 32/33); final closing e2e run was in flight with verifier rescoring at transcript end.

repo: CipherBox node/v3: SealedChildRef (read plane, keyed by ipnsName) vs WriteChildRef (write plane, keyed by node UUID childId) — write-plane operations must key by resolved UUID, never the ipnsName-based caller handle (moveItem's childId param was ipnsName-based, a trap the 68.1-31 planner explicitly caught).

createFolder/publish must include BOTH encryptedIpnsPrivateKey and keyEpoch for TEE republish enrollment — omitting either meant subfolder IPNS records were never enrolled in ipns_republish_schedule and would die at 48h TTL in production.

mock-ipns-routing (delegated routing mock, :3001) keeps records in an in-memory Map — any container restart wipes it; records only survive via the API's ipns_records DB cache written synchronously at publish time. Do NOT restart this container casually during dev testing.

mock-ipns-routing's healthcheck used busybox `wget localhost`, which resolves to ::1 (IPv6) while the app binds IPv4-only — causing perpetual false 'unhealthy' status; fixed to 127.0.0.1 in docker-compose.yml.
API dev server runs on :3000, NOT :3001 (that's the delegated-routing mock) — a source of early false health-probe failures.

apps/web/public/recovery.html (last touched Phase 24) only accepts legacy v2 single-key vault blobs and v2 schema metadata; the app has produced v3/node-v3 blobs since Phase 62 — a real architectural gap needing its own dedicated plan, deliberately deferred with human approval.

shares table's plaintext item_name column was dropped entirely (not renamed) in migration 1750000000000-ApiSchemaCutover, making the REQ-4 itemName backfill permanently dead code (shouldBackfill() always false) — required a product decision (retire vs re-encrypt) rather than a unilateral fix; user chose to remove dead code and redesign using the already-partially-shipped item_name_encrypted/ECIES pipeline.

SharedWriteContext has no ipnsPrivateKey field — shared-write publish keys are derived from inside the unsealed write-body itself, so subfolder write recovery only needs a real writeKey, not independent key recovery.

dfsFindFolder in client.ts unconditionally re-resolved and overwrote every intermediate ancestor's folderTree entry on every call, even already-loaded write-capable ones — root cause of breadcrumb-navigation empty-flash bugs; fixed with a cache short-circuit that reuses already-cached write-capable entries.

Content fileKey vs fileReadKey vs fileWriteKey are three distinct keys (68.1-07 split) — client.downloadFromIpns previously fed the parent folderKey into resolveFileMetadata (which expects the file's OWN readKey), causing AEAD decrypt failures surfaced as 'Decryption failed' in the text editor.

moveItem relinked the read-plane SealedChildRef but left the WriteChildRef orphaned in the SOURCE write-body — files became permanently read-only after being moved into a subfolder (edit/save broken), fixed by re-homing the WriteChildRef under the dest writeKey at destEntry.generation.
Folder-store id desync (UUID vs ipnsName) was the dominant root cause blocking nested-folder creation across most of the originally-17 failing e2e spec groups.

Kind cache (D-02, file-vs-folder discrimination) must be consulted synchronously wherever folder children are inserted/rendered — multiple call sites (FileListItem, ContextMenu, SharedFolderRow, folder.store's SDK-event handler, handleSync, resyncFolder) independently missed wiring it, causing files to render/behave as folders.

batch uploadFiles never inserted WriteChildRefs for uploaded files — every web-uploaded file was un-savable; SharedFolderTree also stored a zeroed writeKey, making every write share silently read-only for recipients.
workflow: GSD wave-based execution: orchestrator stays lean (~15% context), spawns one subagent per plan in worktree isolation, records worktree metadata in a wave manifest, merges after all agents in a wave return, then runs post-merge typecheck + scoped vitest gates before the next wave.

Background long-running subagents (especially those launching a 20+ min e2e suite in a background bash and then pausing to await notification) are prone to 'lost wake' — their session gets evicted and the completion notification never resumes them. Mitigation: arm an independent disk-based watchdog (poll for .last-run.json mtime or similar completion artifact) and use SendMessage to resume the agent with concrete results while its transcript is still warm; if evicted, spawn a fresh continuation agent with explicit completed_state context.

Decision-coverage gate parser requires the tag to be INSIDE the bold ID group: `- **D-04 [informational]:**`, not `- **D-04:** [informational]` — first attempt placing it outside the bold failed silently.
git commits in this repo sometimes report a timeout/failure due to a 1Password integration false-negative — always verify via `git log -1` before assuming a commit failed.

Subagents self-reported and caught their own git-stash violations mid-task (prohibited due to shared refs/stash across worktrees) — recovered via manual reapply rather than stash pop, documented as process incidents in SUMMARY files rather than hidden.

Full 208-spec Playwright suite runs are serial (workers=1) and describe.serial-scoped per file — a failure early in a spec file cascades/aborts all subsequent tests in that file, meaning raw failure counts systematically understate real breakage (many 'failures' are actually 'never executed').

Green e2e suite ≠ every path exercised — deep serial specs that die early structurally never reach later assertions (e.g. text-editor decrypt bug was invisible to the suite until full-workflow reached 6.5.x for the first time after other fixes unblocked earlier steps).

friction: Wave-1 agent stream-stalled mid-execution (~23 min, 119 tool calls) requiring disk spot-check + resume.

Exit-gate agent lost its wake-up after launching the background e2e suite — happened repeatedly across multiple gap rounds (at least 3 distinct occurrences), each requiring manual recovery via watchdog + SendMessage resume or a fresh continuation agent.

Two separate agents hit the account session limit mid-task (once during 68.1-13 continuation, once during 68.1-33 planning), losing in-progress state that had to be recovered from disk and manually validated/committed by the orchestrator.
index.lock contention transiently blocked a tracking commit.
Decision-coverage gate initially failed to parse D-NN bullets (wrong colon placement), requiring investigation of the actual parser source (decisions.cjs) to find the correct format.
A watchdog script polled for a `.last-run.json` file that the playwright config never actually wrote, silently failing to detect suite completion or the associated lost wake.
68.1-21 agent misreported its own `expected_base` in worktree metadata (its own HEAD instead of the true fork point), requiring `git merge-base` verification before recording.
68.1-16 agent ran a prohibited `git stash push` across shared worktree refs, leaving a stray stash entry that had to be carefully identified and dropped without touching the user's own stashes.
User had to manually catch and report two real production bugs (cold-reload navigation, text-editor decryption) that the e2e suite's serial-abort structure had never actually reached/tested.
Extracting live progress from a running background e2e suite was difficult since stdout was piped into the agent's background-task capture rather than a discoverable file.
open_items: Two approved-deferral e2e failures remain out of scope for phase 68.1: recovery.html only supports legacy v2 vault blobs (needs its own gap-closure plan for v3/node-v3 support), and rotation-durability SC-4's replay simulation is unreachable because the API's DB-canonical resolve floor makes stale-record replay untestable (needs an architectural decision or test redesign).

Bin-restore-to-a-different-parent (not the original parent) shares the same WriteChildRef-orphaning bug class as the fixed move bug — documented as a follow-up, not fixed, since the shipped restore-to-original-parent flow is safe.
Ship-time note: commits `17e4319a6` and `7209e8777` have parens beyond conventional-commit scope in their subjects — flagged to keep out of the eventual PR title.
Codebase drift gate reported 143 structural elements since the last codebase mapping (advisory, non-blocking) — recommended a `/gsd-map-codebase` refresh at some point.
Final closing full e2e suite run and verifier rescoring were still in progress at the end of the transcript — phase 68.1 closeout report not yet delivered to the user.
